cornerCallouts: Heading into Turn 1, it's all about carrying maximum speed without compromising the exit.
Turn 2 is crucial for setting up the run down the back straight; a good exit is vital.
Through Turn 3, the drivers will be fighting the car as the banking really starts to bite.
Exiting Turn 4, it's a drag race to the finish line; every tenth of a second counts.
The long run between Turn 4 and Turn 1 offers a prime overtaking opportunity, especially with the tow.
The banking through Turn 3 is significant, testing the limits of the tires and the driver's nerve.
The entry to Turn 1 is deceptively tricky; it's easy to overshoot the braking point.
Turn 2 is a delicate balance between speed and precision; a slight mistake can cost valuable time.
strategyPoints: Tire wear is going to be a major factor today; managing the rubber on this abrasive surface will be key to victory on this 3km oval.
The pit window is relatively short on this oval; a perfectly timed stop can make or break a driver's race.
Fuel consumption will be tight; the drivers will need to balance speed with fuel conservation.
Track position is crucial on an oval; overtaking can be difficult, so qualifying well is essential.
Running high downforce will aid in the corners, but it will hurt top speed on the straights; a compromise is needed.
The draft will be incredibly powerful on this oval, so expect to see plenty of strategic moves.
Look for teams to experiment with different tire pressures to find the optimal balance between grip and longevity.
A late safety car could completely change the complexion of this race, forcing teams to make split-second decisions.
weatherCommentary: The humidity is incredibly high today, making it a real test of physical endurance for the drivers.
The threat of a tropical downpour always looms large over Jacarepaguá; rain could throw a wrench into everyone's plans.
The intense sunshine is baking the track, pushing tire temperatures to the limit.
A slight breeze is coming off the ocean, which might offer some relief to the drivers, but could also affect the car's handling.
The air is thick and heavy, sapping the engines of power and putting extra strain on the cooling systems.
